title: Boss: the sales dashboard
summary: Four honest, labelled charts on one figure.

steps.title: The brief
body: Management wants a one-page sales dashboard. The orders table has `month` (`"2024-01"`...), `region` and
`revenue`, one row per order. You will write one function per chart, each drawing on an `ax` it is given and
returning it, then combine them into a 2 x 2 figure. Writing charts as `f(df, ax)` is what makes them reusable
in any layout. Keep earlier functions as you go; the tests re-check them.

steps.title: The trend
prompt: Write `monthly_line(df, ax)`: total revenue per month (`groupby("month")["revenue"].sum()`), drawn on `ax` as a
line with point markers (`marker="o"`), title `Monthly revenue`, x label `Month`, y label `Revenue`. Return `ax`.
template: Dojo.eq("monthly totals", [round(float(v), 1) for v in dojo_orders.groupby("month")["revenue"].sum()], [round(float(v), 1) for v in _a.get_lines()[0].get_ydata()] if _a.get_lines() else [])

steps.title: The comparison
prompt: Add `region_bars(df, ax)`: total revenue per region as bars **sorted highest first**, y axis from zero, title
steps.starter:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


def monthly_line(df, ax):
    monthly = df.groupby("month")["revenue"].sum()
    ax.plot(monthly.index, monthly.values, marker="o")
    ax.set(title="Monthly revenue", xlabel="Month", ylabel="Revenue")
    return ax
template: Dojo.eq("bar heights", [float(v) for v in _exp], [float(p.get_height()) for p in _a.patches])

steps.title: The distribution
prompt: Add `order_histogram(df, ax)`: a histogram of the order `revenue` with 8 bins, title `Order values`, x label
steps.starter:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


def monthly_line(df, ax):
    monthly = df.groupby("month")["revenue"].sum()
    ax.plot(monthly.index, monthly.values, marker="o")
    ax.set(title="Monthly revenue", xlabel="Month", ylabel="Revenue")
    return ax


def region_bars(df, ax):
    totals = df.groupby("region")["revenue"].sum().sort_values(ascending=False)
    ax.bar(totals.index, totals.values)
    ax.set_ylim(0, None)
    ax.set(title="Revenue by region", ylabel="Revenue")
    return ax
template: Dojo.eq("all 24 orders counted", 24, int(sum(p.get_height() for p in _a.patches)))

steps.title: The dashboard
prompt: Add `dashboard(df)` returning `(fig, axes)` for a 2 x 2 figure titled `Sales dashboard` (`fig.suptitle`):
- top left: `monthly_line`, top right: `region_bars`, bottom left: `order_histogram`,
- bottom right: box plots of order revenue per region, regions in sorted order as tick labels,
steps.starter:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


def monthly_line(df, ax):
    monthly = df.groupby("month")["revenue"].sum()
    ax.plot(monthly.index, monthly.values, marker="o")
    ax.set(title="Monthly revenue", xlabel="Month", ylabel="Revenue")
    return ax


def region_bars(df, ax):
    totals = df.groupby("region")["revenue"].sum().sort_values(ascending=False)
    ax.bar(totals.index, totals.values)
    ax.set_ylim(0, None)
    ax.set(title="Revenue by region", ylabel="Revenue")
    return ax


def order_histogram(df, ax):
    ax.hist(df["revenue"], bins=8)
    ax.set(title="Order values", xlabel="Revenue", ylabel="Orders")
    return ax
